summary: # Marvelous Designer: Learning Day - Ancient Greek Costume Making Tutorial Part 2 - Q&A Session ## Introduction In this session, we will address various questions related to the process of making ancient Greek costumes using Marvelous Designer. The focus will be on tying legs, understanding measurements, and troubleshooting common issues encountered while using the software. ## How to Tie Your Legs **Question:** How to tie your legs? **Response:** Legs... What is how to tie your legs? Don't you know how to tie this board? It's... You don't know how to tie this line, right? ## Understanding Measurements ### Basic Measurements - **Basicocentrometer**: This is a fundamental measurement tool. Let me show you several types: - **Basicocentrometer**: This is a circle measurement. - **Surface Circumference**: This measurement sticks to the body. It will go in. - **Basic Circumference**: This does not stick to the body; it selects the most prominent point in the middle and connects it to the line. ### Dress Fitting Generally speaking, this dress will not stick to the body. However, sometimes it is more special. For example, a coat will stick to your body. In certain situations, you may want it to stick and connect to the line. ### Length Measurement - **Why Not Use Circle Measurement?**: The basic length measurement is used because a whole circle measurement cannot stick properly. - **Setting Positions**: Set two positions for length measurement. After setting these, the length measurement is one-stop. ### Stability of the Model When you stick a long board to it for a whole section, it can easily become unstable. So, I will cut out a section in the middle and stick the cut section to it. This way, it won’t move back and forth; it will be fixed here. ## Arm and Wrist Measurements - For the arm and wrist, for example, the sleeve and shoe cuff, you have to lock it in the wrist position. Then, we will create a board for it. After sticking it here, I will simulate it. It is a circle. ### Gravity Simulation In this simulation, it will be stuck here and won’t move, unaffected by gravity. If your arm is bent, the sleeve may fall down. However, it will be fixed here and won’t fall. ## Floating Effect of the Sleeve ### What is the Floating Effect? Some people want to achieve a floating effect for the sleeve. In 2D cartoons, sleeves can be large yet remain in place. This tool can lock it here, and you can increase the conflict thickness to create a floating effect. ### Practical Application - Increasing conflict thickness a little bit gives a floating effect. For example, there is a ring on the arm. - Have you learned it? ## Troubleshooting and Compatibility Issues - **TFT Model Compatibility**: Some users face issues where the TFT model is not compatible. Your face may differ. - **Fixing the Wrist**: If the wrist measurement is not clear, it needs to be very stiff. ### Using Conflict Thickness - If the effect is meant to be floating, you can use this TFT model to fix it. After applying conflict thickness, it can maintain its shape. ## Additional Q&A ### Virtual Model Transparency - **How to Make a Virtual Model Transparent?**: Press Shift + X to toggle transparency. ### Importing Models - OBJ and FBX formats can be imported into Marvelous Designer. If you have issues with FBX, you can export it as OBJ. ### Upcoming Tutorials - For more tutorials, please follow our Bilibili account, mdguanfang, where live broadcasts will be posted. ### Special Requests and Suggestions - If you have requests for specific tutorials like making a folding umbrella or other topics, please message us or join our QQ group. ## Conclusion Thank you for your questions and support for our software! If you have any further inquiries, feel free to join our QQ group for technical support. See you in the next teaching video!
